concepts.title: Distance Formula
concepts.definition: The distance between points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) equals the square root of (x2 - x1) squared plus (y2 - y1) squared - the Pythagorean theorem applied to the coordinate plane.
concepts.key_idea: Coordinate gaps are the legs; the distance is the hypotenuse.
question_patterns: find the distance between the points (3, 4) and (0, 0)
calculate the distance between the two given points
show that the given points form a right triangle using distances
find a point on the x-axis equidistant from the two given points
which of the given points is farthest from the origin
determine whether the given points are collinear using distances

solution_steps.explain: Square the gaps, add, and take the square root.

concepts.title: Section Formula
concepts.definition: The coordinates of the point dividing the join of (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) in the ratio m : n internally are ((m x2 + n x1) over (m + n), (m y2 + n y1) over (m + n)); the midpoint is the special case m = n.
concepts.key_idea: Weights swap sides: the farther ratio pulls the point toward the opposite endpoint.
question_patterns: find the coordinates of the point dividing the join in the ratio m : n
find the midpoint of the segment joining the given points
in what ratio does the point divide the given segment
find the point that trisects the given segment
check whether the given point lies on the segment and in what ratio
use the section formula to find the missing coordinate

solution_steps.explain: m times x2 plus n times x1, over m + n.
Same weights applied to the y-values.

concepts.title: Area of a Triangle from Its Vertices
concepts.definition: The area of a triangle with vertices (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (x3, y3) equals half the absolute value of x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2); a zero result means the three points are collinear.
concepts.key_idea: Three vertices in, one area out: zero area exposes collinearity.
question_patterns: find the area of the triangle whose vertices are given
check whether the given three points are collinear using the area formula
find the value of k for which the points are collinear
calculate the area of the triangle formed by the given points
compare the areas of the two given triangles from their vertices
why does the area formula use the absolute value - explain

solution_steps.explain: Compute x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2).
The area is the absolute value of det over 2.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find the distance between the points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2).

solution_template.explain: m x2 plus n x1 over m + n.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A segment joins (x1, y1) to (x2, y2). Find the y-coordinate of its point of division in the ratio {m} : {n}.
Find the area of the triangle with vertices (x1, y1), (x2, y2) and (x3, y3).

solution_template.explain: Sum the three products of coordinates.
The area is half the magnitude.

solution_template.explain: The coordinate products decide the area.
